chose: make per-change pressure a fingerprinted signal gate with an explicit no-new-invariant attestation
over: turn every novelty advisory into a hard failure
search arbitrary journal prose for a waiver
because: only zero-anchor behavioral growth needs an immediate choice; a content fingerprint invalidates the waiver when the patch changes, while a structured finding key makes the decision addressable and deduplicated

chose: run per-change signaling at Stop/SubagentStop and collect read traces at PostToolUse
over: run a full graph/worktree analysis after every edit tool call
leave calibration as a manual report with no observation source
because: stop time is once per agent change and still early enough to add an anchor or attest; PostToolUse is cheap enough for append-only path observations but too frequent for structural analysis

chose: commit calibration samples as one append-only file per agent session while keeping raw read traces transient
over: keep all calibration local and lose the empirical record on a fresh clone
append every agent to one committed calibration.jsonl
because: paths, predicted sets and labeled outcomes are the evidence used to calibrate the metric and must survive; raw tool events are noisy/private plumbing, while per-session sample files preserve concurrent writes and clean merges like the decision journal

chose: bind hook traces and journal sessions to the host's agent identifier
over: key every subagent by the parent session identifier
because: Claude tool hooks carry agent_id inside subagents; session_id would merge concurrent readers and make per-agent calibration false

chose: give lifecycle hooks a dependency-light executable
over: route every PostToolUse event through the full CLI registry
because: five measured launches took 0.35s through hook-cli versus 1.28s through cli; the high-frequency observer must not recreate the read-cost gradient

chose: eager CLI imports dominate the hook's avoidable startup cost
because: 30 launches measured median 65.1 ms (p90 70.3) through hook-cli versus median 256.5 ms (p90 264.0) through the full CLI; lazy Stop imports remove the eager command and TypeScript analysis stack from PostToolUse

chose: a real calibration attribution error; the acceptance signal's patch-wide scope is intentional
because: the host supplies agent_id on subagent tool events; traces and calibration now prefer that id, and the concurrent-union unit test proves explicit session writes exclude another agent's changed path. The Stop signal deliberately remains worktree-wide because CI accepts the combined patch, while calibration no longer misattributes that union to one reader

chose: emit Stop signaling once and stay silent when stop_hook_active is true
over: re-emit the same journal and signal feedback on every follow-up stop
because: Stop additionalContext creates a feedback turn; without the host flag guard the non-failing nudge repeats until the host's hard cap and becomes the expensive gate the journal rejects

chose: carry the host agent identity on every injected journal verb, including resolutions and dismissals
over: use only the session id and let later writes default to agent main
because: a unique file prevents write collisions but does not preserve who made the decision; the lifecycle payload already supplies agent_type, so dropping it would make structurally separated subagent records semantically unattributed
